page.layout: One page of text. At the top, a printed page number at left and a woodcut frieze (ornament, not text). Below it, a centred title block in several lines, then a verse passage with a large woodcut initial R. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.head: PAVLI MELISSI FRANCI COMITIS SACRI PALAT. ET EQVIT. CIVIS ROM. carmen ad Ioannem Ia-comotum Bar-rensem.

p.i: REGES ut alto stemmate prosatos, Vivas Deorum Cœlitum imagines In orbe miramur, sacrisque Deserimus meritæ[?] honorum Laudes tiaris, si propriè imperent, Nec execranda regna Tyrannide Quassata vertant, & profuso Sanguine triste solum cruentent. Sic & poetas suspicere est pium Industrioso pectore præditos Regum incinentes[?] fortiorum Prælia, magnanimasque vires, Christi tuendo pro grege, pro fide Sanctè adserenda, proque animæ bonis, Saluteq[?] ipsa vindicanda: Inter eos IACOMOTE postus,

page.notes: Woodcut floral frieze above the title, and a large decorated initial R at the start of the verse, both ornament only. The page number 124 is printed at the top left. Catchword "Ceu" printed at the lower right. Doubtful readings: "meritæ" (abbreviation mark uncertain), "incinentes", "Saluteq" (the q-ligature is unclear), and "postus". The first line of the verse is set with the large initial R joined to the word "EGES", written here as REGES. The verse is set in italic with small capitals in the first word and in IACOMOTE. Verse lines are kept within one paragraph, as one stanza.
